title: Reaction–diffusion
description: Paint and watch patterns evolve in a Gray–Scott simulation. Two substances react and diffuse across a 256 × 256 grid. Compute shaders update their concentrations, then a render pass colors the result.
paint: Paint with a mouse or touch to inject substance B. Painting also works while paused.
unavailable: WebGPU is unavailable in this environment.
lost: The GPU device was lost. Reload the page to restart.
substances: Each cell holds the concentrations of A and B. These substances diffuse to neighboring cells and react with each other, consuming A to produce B. Opposite edges of the grid are connected.
parametersHelp: The feed and removal controls determine how much A enters the system and how much B leaves it. Adjusting this balance produces different patterns. Each preset starts from the same nine seeds with new parameters.
pingPong: The simulation uses two textures, each holding both A and B. At each step, it reads the state from one and writes the result to the other. The textures then swap roles for the next step, so a pass never reads and writes the same texture.
brushHelp: Before simulation, a dedicated compute pass injects B into a disk with a radius of six cells. The disk wraps across the grid edges. You can also paint while paused without advancing the reaction.
colorHelp: The palette turns the concentration of B into color without changing the simulation. Choose the A or B grayscale view to inspect the concentrations directly.
speedHelp: Speed controls how many steps run each frame, from 1 to 16. Each step uses the same numerical timestep, but the overall pace also depends on the browser’s frame rate. This is not a duration in physical seconds. Use Pause and One step to follow the changes one iteration at a time.
